column1: # Dispositioned formal task directories: the ones whose non-PASS verdict
# is a decision this project has already made and recorded, rather than a
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/verify.sh counts every directory holding a
# config.sby and a logfile.txt and classifies it PASS / FAIL / ERROR /
# STOPPED / STALE / UNCHECKED. Its own header refuses to whitelist
# anything inside that counter -- "an allowlist maintained inside a
# counter is how a counter starts lying, and this file exists because of
# one that did" -- and says what it wants instead:
#   "If the project wants a green gate it has to first decide, in a
#    tracked artefact, which of the thirty-five are expected -- and that
#    is a decision about the formal work, not about this script."
# This is that artefact. It changes NO count. `formal_other` in
# verification-log.tsv stays the true number of non-PASS directories, and
# always will. What it adds is a second number, `formal_undispositioned`,
# which is the one the exit code gates on -- so a NEW non-PASS directory
# turns the gate red while these stay amber and counted.
# WHAT A ROW MEANS. A row says: this directory's verdict is expected, a
# named document section says why, and someone decided to leave it. It
# does NOT say the check passes, that the underlying question is settled,
# or that the work behind it is done. docs/63 section 11 lists the routes
# out of the two largest groups and none of them is free.
# WHAT MAKES A ROW GO STALE, and both directions are checked:
#   * the directory now PASSES -- the disposition is a hole, delete it;
#   * the directory's verdict CHANGED to a different non-PASS word --
#     STOPPED becoming FAIL is a new fact and this file must not absorb
# EVERY ROW HERE IS UNDER hw/soc/out/rvf*, the vendored Ibex
# riscv-formal runs. Not one is in this project's own property sets
# (formal/ and hw/soc/formal/), which are 54 and 64 PASS with nothing
# else, and that is the property worth keeping true: the day a row in
# this file names a directory under formal/ or hw/soc/formal/, something
# has gone wrong with what this project itself proves.
